comparison_to_one_swap.one_swap_input: continuous raw frames 0..29 at stride 1; current frame 30
comparison_to_one_swap.important_distribution_shift: The learned 30-position temporal embedding saw reveal at positions 0..9, cover at 10..19, and swap_0 at 20..29. Under frame59/stride2 it sees about five positions per phase: reveal 0..5, cover 6..10, swap_0 11..15, swap_1 16..20, swap_2 21..25, settle 26..29.
comparison_to_one_swap.optimization_difference: The successful one-swap curriculum used separate 500-step temporal and 500-step memory stages followed by 200 low-LR joint steps. The three-swap diagnostic attempted a 150-step readout and a 300-step high-LR joint update over 147.35M parameters.

most_likely_causes: one-swap training learns a fixed phase-specific mapping rather than a reusable state-update operation
stride-2 sampling halves the observations per swap and changes apparent motion speed
learned absolute temporal positions undergo a major phase-alignment distribution shift
two factorized temporal/spatial blocks may be too shallow for three sequential identity updates
the three-swap joint optimization changes too many parameters at once and does not reproduce the successful staged curriculum
